text: What Isaac knows is nowhere said. He carries the wood; he asks concerning the lamb; from Abraham he receives words which answer the sound of his question and evade its meaning. Of Isaac's inward thought or feeling there is no disclosure. The narrator gives only the action, that they went, both of them, together; and when the phrase returns in Genesis 22, the repetition does the work of exposition. The question of Isaac's consent has been raised, but is suffered to fall. In this account, the logic of Obedience settles the whole reckoning, and leaves nothing unaccounted for.
